# Registry fixture provenance

`index.json` in this directory is a real, verifiable Ed25519-signed
registry index, generated by a standalone Go program (not by this
package's own production code) using the standard library's
`crypto/ed25519` — the same primitive `pkg/plugin`'s `Ed25519Verifier`
checks against in production.

- Tool: Go standard library `crypto/ed25519` (module Go toolchain, see
  `go.mod` for the pinned Go version).
- Date generated: 2026-09-07.
- Generation method: a throwaway `go run` program (not committed) built
  an Ed25519 key from a fixed 32-byte seed, JSON-marshaled two entries
  plus `schema_version`, computed the signed payload exactly as
  `Ed25519Verifier.VerifyIndex` reconstructs it (`schema_version` plus the
  raw `entries` bytes, re-encoded via `encoding/json`), signed that
  payload with `ed25519.Sign`, and wrote the envelope
  `{schema_version, entries, signature}` with the base64-encoded
  signature to `index.json`.
- Public key (base64, standard encoding): the corresponding
  `ed25519.PublicKey` is embedded directly in `client_test.go` (constant
  `testRegistryPublicKeyB64`) so the fixture and its verifying key travel
  together and a reviewer can re-derive one from the other.

## Why Ed25519 rather than the minisign wire format

The ticket's prose describes a detached minisign v2 signature: a separate
`index.json.minisig` file in minisign's own armored text format
(untrusted-comment line, base64 `Ed<8-byte key ID><64-byte signature>`
line, trusted-comment line, base64 global signature line), fetched
alongside `index.json` via a second HTTP request.

The actual contract surface this ticket was told to implement against —
`pkg/plugin/registry.go`, landed by an earlier ticket and declared
authoritative over the ticket's own file layout — has no second
artifact to fetch: `RegistryFetcher.FetchIndex` returns exactly one
`[]byte`, and `RegistryIndex.Signature` is a field embedded in the same
JSON document it signs, not a sibling file. There is no method on
`RegistryFetcher` to retrieve a second, detached signature blob.

Implementing full minisign wire-format parsing (key IDs, trusted
comments, the untrusted-comment convention, `BLAKE2b` pre-hashing for
large files) against a shape that structurally cannot carry a second
artifact would be dishonest complexity: the parser would exist, but
nothing in the real fetch path could ever hand it the second file
minisign's format assumes. `Ed25519Verifier` instead performs real,
standard, unforgeable Ed25519 signature verification (the same primitive
minisign itself uses under the hood) directly over the embedded
`signature` field, using the standard library only — no custom crypto,
no CGO. This is recorded as a contract-vs-tree contradiction in the
ticket's journal, with both sides quoted.
